data.name: BLACK ART
data.detailed_description:
BLACK ART is an art-driven action-adventure journey set in a striking world where three distinct aesthetics—Cyberpunk, Steampunk, and Ruinpunk—meet on the streets. As a rebel artist, you carry the power to transform your surroundings. Leave your mark, bring color to the gray, and redefine the city's soul through your art.

Key Gameplay Features:

  • The Fusion of Three Worlds: Explore an atmospheric blend of neon glows, industrial steampunk textures, and the silent beauty of rusty ruins.

  • Dynamic Art Mechanics: Every wall is a potential canvas. Use your spray cans and posters to change the visual landscape of the city in real-time.

  • Reclaiming the Streets: As you decorate the environment, watch the cold and abandoned atmosphere evolve into a vibrant space filled with your creative energy.

  • Atmospheric Discovery: Navigate through Punk districts, finding the perfect spots to express your vision.

  • Custom Character Designs: Encounter 3D characters inspired by these three genres, each manually refined to fit the game's unique artistic direction.

data.short_description: BLACK ART is an art-driven action-adventure game set in a dystopian world. Blending Cyberpunk, Steampunk, and Ruinpunk, you play as a rebel artist defying authority by hanging posters and spraying graffiti. Leave your artistic mark amidst rusty ruins and neon lights!

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • Requires a 64-bit processor and operating system
  • OS: Windows 11 (64-bit)
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-12400 / AMD Ryzen 5 5600X
  • Memory: 16 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA RTX 3060 / RX 6600 XT
  • DirectX: Version 12
  • Network: Broadband Internet connection

content_descriptors.notes: BLACK ART is set in a dystopian universe blending cyberpunk and steampunk themes. The game explores mature themes such as social rebellion, defiance of authority (expressed through actions like street art, graffiti, and hanging posters), and the pervasive dark, mature atmosphere inherent to this world.
